title: ₹60,000 School Fee: School Chalane Wale Ke Paas Kitna Bachta Hai?
description: The pump-owner reels with 1.8M and 2.7M views show people click to learn where the owner's money really comes from. Schools are a classic dream business with almost no public insider explanation. Our preschool reel doesn't cover the full CBSE school.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: Economics of a mid-size private CBSE school (India)

Heads-up for the scriptwriter: I found no audited P&L of a real 1,000-student CBSE school. Schools are non-profits and don't publish one. The walk-through in Section 3 is therefore arithmetic on sourced inputs, labelled as such. Rent paid to promoters, vendor margins and the owners' actual take have no public rupee figures. Don't put a number on them in the script.

**1. LEGAL STRUCTURE (the "non-profit" hook)**
- The RTE Act 2009 mandates that schools run under a non-profit entity: a Public Charitable Trust, Registered Society or Section 8 Company. [https://www.raysolute.com/school-governance-trust-society-section8.html]
- CBSE bye-laws say societies/trusts/companies must run schools without any profit motive. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- No capitation fee or admission donation is allowed. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- For-profit companies cannot hold school affiliations. [https://www.raysolute.com/school-governance-trust-society-section8.html]
- A family trust created for personal profit is not suitable. [https://schoolnaukri.com/blog/who-can-apply-for-cbse-affiliation-society-trust-company-government-school-rules]
- The entity should be registered for 3+ years in most cases. This is a third-party reading of the bye-laws, with some exemptions. [https://www.raysolute.com/school-governance-trust-society-section8.html]
- The Supreme Court line is "profit yes, profiteering no." In Modern School v. Union of India (2004), the Court upheld a "reasonable surplus" for development and expansion but said autonomy must not lead to commercialisation. [https://scroll.in/article/801525/who-should-decide-the-fees-charged-by-private-schools]
- One judge separately put a reasonable surplus ordinarily at 6–15%. This is a commentary source on a separate opinion. [https://kbssidhu.substack.com/p/private-universities-fees-a-cushion]
- Tax rule: a trust claims exemption if it applies at least 85% of income to approved purposes in India. [https://www.axismaxlife.com/blog/tax-savings/section-11-income-tax-act-1961]
- It may accumulate the other 15% without conditions. [https://www.axismaxlife.com/blog/tax-savings/section-11-income-tax-act-1961]
- Surplus beyond what can be accumulated becomes taxable. [https://madurai-icai.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Practical-issues-and-recent-development_compressed-1.pdf]

**2. WHAT IT COSTS TO START**

Land (rules vary by city and have changed over time)
- Older bye-laws: about two acres, with the building on part of the land and playgrounds on the rest. [https://www.cbse.gov.in/examin~1/Affiliation%20Bye%20Laws%20Word%20(Final)%20for%20uploading%20on%20the%20website_2012.pdf]
- 2018 bye-laws, per a reproduction site: land of not less than 6,000 sq m can be accepted if the minimum of 8,000 sq m isn't met, with limits on enrolment and sections. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- Same source: a 4,000 sq m minimum applies in certain cases, and hill-station schools need 2,000 sq m for secondary. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- Big cities: NOIDA, Ghaziabad, Gurugram, Mohali, Chandigarh and cities above 1.5 million need at least 4,000 sq m (0.99 acres) for senior secondary. [https://www.schoolserv.in/land-and-infrastructure-required-for-cbse-affiliation/]
- The land must be one contiguous plot. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- Title documents must be in the name of the school/society/trust/company. [https://www.schoolserv.in/cbse-affiliation-bye-laws-2018/]
- If the land is leased, the lease must be at least 15 years. [https://www.schoolserv.in/land-and-infrastructure-required-for-cbse-affiliation/]
- The lessor must own the land. Sub-leases are not accepted. [https://www.rajeevelt.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/CBSE-AFFILIATION-REQUIRED-DOCUMENTS-AND-CHECKLIST-FOR-SCHOOL-FROM-www-cbseaff-nic-in.pdf]
- 2026 change, per a consultant guide: the number of sections a school can run is now decided by total built-up carpet area, not just land area. [https://www.rijadeja.com/cbse/bye-laws/]
- Land price in ₹: no reliable figure found. It depends on the city.

Building and equipment
- A CBSE school costs ₹9–20 crore for Phase 1, ex-land. [https://www.raysolute.com/cost-of-setting-up-a-school-in-india.html]
- Tier-2 city: ₹9–15 crore ex-land. Metro premium: ₹14–28 crore ex-land. [https://www.raysolute.com/cost-of-setting-up-a-school-in-india.html]
- Land typically adds another 30–40% on top. [https://www.raysolute.com/cost-of-setting-up-a-school-in-india.html]
